paper_title: Searches for signatures of ultra-light axion dark matter in polarimetry data of the European Pulsar Timing Array
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1 (y-axis plotted as g_agamma/(10^-12 GeV^-1); axis multiplier 10^-12 applied)
notes: EPTA pulsar polarimetry search for ultra-light ALP-induced birefringence, constraining g_agamma over ma = 6e-24 to 5e-21 eV. Only spot values are given in text: frequentist best limit g95 ~ 4e-14 GeV^-1 at ma ~ 8e-24 eV (Sec. V.A; note the Conclusions section inconsistently quotes 5e-13 GeV^-1 at the same mass), and Bayesian conservative best limit g95 = 2e-13 GeV^-1 at ma = 3e-23 eV. Full exclusion curves are only in Figs. 7 and 10 (not machine-readable here), so data_points are sparse anchor values; the limit degrades roughly proportional to ma toward higher masses. Local DM density assumed rho = 0.4 GeV/cm^3 at both Earth and pulsar; stochastic Rayleigh-distributed field amplitudes included. A signal found near 1-2e-8 Hz is attributed to residual ionospheric Faraday rotation, not ALPs. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 46)) | Vision: Traced the solid gray 'Bayesian' (conservative) 95% upper limit in Fig. 7.
